findings.title: Default Tiny recovery still loses eligibility when failed download cleanup removes its canonical ZIP.
findings.trigger: Successfully construct/read Tiny through the canonical default URL, delete only one of two referenced validation PNGs while retaining directories/annotations/training and the original ZIP/completion, then make the recovery source return HTTP 503 for all three normal retry attempts. Restore the same HTTP source to the original complete ZIP and construct again. Invalid archive bodies trigger the same issue.
findings.actual: Recovery invalidates .complete under flock. The downloader deletes tiny-imagenet-200.zip on the first HTTP error (and after invalid archive extraction), then exhausts retries. The next constructor waits/acquires the guard but sees neither ZIP nor completion and raises the incomplete-native ValueError at tiny_imagenet.py:78. It sends no request to the now-restored source; required PNG remains absent. Default observation: four total requests (one success plus three failures), zero successful retry constructors, no completion, no canonical ZIP. Equivalent configured-source control: five requests, successful restored-source constructor, correct labels/finite sample access and offline reuse.
findings.expected: A root recognized as a prior default download stays eligible to retry after a bounded failed recovery when the source works again. Incomplete data must remain unmarked. Manual incomplete native/unlabeled roots lacking default artifacts still reject, and a generic lock/unrelated archive remains insufficient.
findings.impact: A transient HTTP outage while repairing one lost required image makes a previously default-downloaded dataset persistently unusable until manual intervention or configuration changes. The source can be healthy yet is never retried.

findings.required_fix: Preserve recognized default-source recovery eligibility through existing download-error cleanup under the same guard, while keeping incomplete completion absent. A bounded approach can retain the prior canonical archive while staging replacement attempts; do not rely on a generic lock, broaden acceptance of arbitrary manual native roots, or introduce a corpus manifest/new format/protocol. Add actual HTTP-error/invalid-archive -> restored-source constructor regressions on both versions, with configured and offline/labels/unknown-class/contention controls retained. Coordinate any necessary bounded downloader change with its existing owner.
findings.scope_and_attribution: Remaining R2A-04/R2A3-01 default recovery correctness coupled to unchanged base downloader cleanup, not a claim that request cleanup was newly added in 5f4749d. Original failed-readiness and successful contention reproductions pass. HTTP 503 performs no extraction or filesystem-corruption rollback, so this finding does not expand accepted archive rollback limits. Invalid archive is corroboration of the same eligibility loss, not a separate containment finding.
findings.routing: Original author fixes this bounded material issue, then another fresh independent exact-candidate review. Do not rewrite earlier reports/verdicts or treat this review as root acceptance.

harness_disposition.initial_provision: Initial 3.13 uv call used --no-managed-python, which excluded the already-installed uv-managed interpreter and exited 2 before installing. Corrected by supplying its exact existing interpreter path. Initial log retained; no product failure or candidate edit.
harness_disposition.initial_coupled: Initial coupled probe expected BadZipFile for a non-ZIP response; extract_archive detects non-ZIP and tries TAR, raising caught tarfile.ReadError after three retries. Those two bad_zip initial failures are excluded as harness failures. The HTTP default product failure already reproduced; other five nodes passed. Initial script/logs/JUnit/fixtures are retained unchanged.
harness_disposition.corrected_coupled: Separate corrected script permits precisely BadZipFile or tarfile.ReadError for failed invalid-archive recovery; all retry/readiness/marker/sample assertions remain. Both versions then show only the two actual default-source restored-retry ValueErrors, with six controls passing. No product red was reclassified as green or suppressed.
harness_disposition.finding_cardinality: HTTP and invalid-archive triggers are one shared material finding. Original/independent/coupled counts overlap; no totals across suites.
